title: The Faithful Atlas
premise: In the river city of Vhalen, on the eve of a revolution that will decide whether the provinces break from the Empire, Kestrel Zhou secretly prints seditious pamphlets in her father's type shop while learning which silences keep people alive. When the season's floods close the only bridge out of the city, she becomes the reluctant courier between a rebel cell and an imperial officer who once loved her mother — and whose mercy may be the family's only escape. As the armistice negotiations stall and reprisals begin, Kestrel discovers there is one berth left on the last barge across the closed bridge: enough passage for her father or her brother, not both. She forges a document naming herself instead, sacrificing her own safety to spare them the choice, and in the final chapter watches the armistice signed over a city she saved at the cost of everything she was.
about_author: Ivo Kavanagh is the pen name of a former letterpress restorer who spent a decade cataloguing printing houses in border towns before turning to fiction. The Faithful Atlas is their second novel, drawn from family letters smuggled out during an unnamed civil conflict.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Kestrel Zhou sorts type in her father's print shop, memorizing which customers' orders must never be discussed aloud. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: quiet vigilance — we see a girl who has made silence into a craft.

chapters.title: What the River Brings
chapters.summary: A stranger leaves a sealed packet among the jobbing work; Kestrel's father burns it unread, but she has already read it. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: first crack in the family's careful neutrality.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Knew Her Mother
chapters.summary: Imperial Captain Aldous Vey inspects the shop and lingers over a portrait of Kestrel's dead mother. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: ambiguous menace — he knows more than he says.

chapters.title: Apprentice to Secrets
chapters.summary: Her brother Tam reveals he has joined the printers' cell; Kestrel covers for him before their father notices. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling her toward danger she swore to avoid.

chapters.title: Rain on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Autumn storms begin; officials announce the bridge will close within the fortnight. The city's mood turns feverish. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: dread of enclosure — the trap closing.

chapters.title: The First Pamphlet
chapters.summary: Kestrel sets forbidden type alone at night, hands shaking, and prints two hundred copies of a call to strike. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Tea with the Captain
chapters.summary: Vey returns, ostensibly about a tax stamp, and quotes her mother's handwriting from memory. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: seduction of the past as a weapon.

chapters.title: Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel finds her father's hidden accounts: he has been paying protection to both sides for years. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: disillusionment — survival has its own quiet corruptions.

chapters.title: The Cell Meets
chapters.summary: In a cellar beneath the chandlery, Kestrel meets the cell: a schoolteacher, a dockhand, a widow. They argue strategy while the river rises. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: fragile fellowship.

chapters.title: Closed
chapters.summary: The bridge shuts for the season with iron chains and soldiers. News stops; rumors multiply. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the city becomes a held breath.

chapters.title: The Widow's Request
chapters.summary: Cell member Marta asks Kestrel to print death-notices for executed strikers under false names. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into defiance.

chapters.title: Vey's Offer
chapters.summary: Vey privately offers Kestrel's family safe conduct papers — if she names the cell's leader. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: Tam's Mistake
chapters.summary: Tam distributes pamphlets too near a garrison post; a boy is arrested carrying one. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: guilt and the cost of zealotry.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: The arrested boy's sister comes to the shop begging help; Kestrel's father refuses, Kestrel does not. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the moment neutrality dies.

chapters.title: The Atlas of Safe Houses
chapters.summary: Kestrel draws a hand-inked map of every sympathetic household — the 'faithful atlas' of the title — and distributes copies. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: agency found through craft.

chapters.title: Snow Over the Barracks
chapters.summary: Vey, ordered to escalate reprisals, delays his report by three days — an act of quiet treason. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: the officer discovering his own divided heart.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Chandlery
chapters.summary: A raid catches the schoolteacher; someone informed. Suspicion poisons the cell. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: paranoia's corrosive spread.

chapters.title: Which Silence
chapters.summary: Kestrel realizes her father may be the informant, buying safety with names. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: horror — the protector as betrayer.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Press
chapters.summary: Father and daughter clash over the ledger; he admits paying, denies informing, and she cannot tell truth from survival. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: love strained past recognition.

chapters.title: The Armistice Envoy
chapters.summary: An imperial envoy arrives to negotiate with provincial leaders; the whole city waits on words. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous rumor.

chapters.title: Terms and Treasons
chapters.summary: Negotiations stall over amnesty lists; the rebels demand names, the Empire demands surrender of the printers. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: the machinery of compromise grinding lives.

chapters.title: Marta's Choice
chapters.summary: Marta volunteers to surrender herself as a decoy printer so the real press can move. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely given, devastatingly received.

chapters.title: Moving the Type
chapters.summary: Kestrel smuggles the press piece by piece through flooded streets to the salt warehouse. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: exhausted determination.

chapters.title: The Last Berth Announced
chapters.summary: Vey reveals one berth remains on a supply barge crossing the closed bridge before the armistice concludes — one person out. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: mercy offered as an impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Family Arithmetic
chapters.summary: The Zhous face the choice: father, son, or daughter. Each insists another take it. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: love expressed as refusal.

chapters.title: Tam Volunteers
chapters.summary: Tam claims the berth, arguing his life is worth most to the cause; Kestrel sees he is also fleeing guilt. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: courage tangled with cowardice.

chapters.title: The Forged Manifest
chapters.summary: Alone at night, Kestrel alters the manifest to name herself, erasing her family from the record entirely. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as the ultimate act of authorship.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Vey finds the forgery and understands what she has done — and why. He says nothing, yet. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: complicity born of tenderness.

chapters.title: The Informer Named
chapters.summary: The true informant is exposed: not the father, but the widow's lodger. The cell's rage nearly kills an innocent. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: relief curdling into shame.

chapters.title: Reprisals Begin
chapters.summary: With talks failing, garrisons burn the chandlery; Marta is taken. The city arms itself. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Kestrel goes to the bridge to board the barge; Vey meets her there and tears up the manifest, ordering her back — then gives her his own pass instead. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth — she refuses to leave without her brother.

chapters.title: The Bridge Stands Open
chapters.summary: Kestrel uses Vey's pass to force the gate open for fleeing families, not just one berth; soldiers waver, then stand aside. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: one small mercy multiplying beyond design.

chapters.title: What Vey Surrenders
chapters.summary: Vey reports the bridge 'breached by mob action,' destroying his career to bury the evidence against the Zhous. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: ruin accepted as penance and gift.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: The armistice is signed; amnesty is broad but imperfect. Names are read aloud in the square — some living, some not. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: victory that tastes of ash.

chapters.title: Marta's Name
chapters.summary: Marta is not on the amnesty list; Kestrel prints ten thousand copies of her name until authorities relent. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the press as memorial.

chapters.title: Father's Hands
chapters.summary: Her father, broken by the revelations, returns to setting type — honest work, plainly declared. Reconciliation without absolution. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: forgiveness as ongoing labor.

chapters.title: Letters Across the Water
chapters.summary: Tam writes from exile in the provinces; Kestrel answers in code only siblings would know. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: distance bridged by shared language.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Kestrel reopens the print shop under her own name, the atlas of safe houses framed behind the counter. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: claiming inheritance on her own terms.

chapters.title: Vey's Last Visit
chapters.summary: Vey, dismissed and departing, buys a blank book from her — paper for whatever confession he owes. They part without forgiveness, with understanding. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: two survivors honoring what cannot be repaired.

chapters.title: The Faithful Atlas
chapters.summary: Years later, Kestrel teaches an apprentice which silences keep people safe — and which truths must be printed anyway. The atlas hangs open, still being added to. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: resolution — survival's price paid forward as memory.
